name: contribution_creation_groups
description: Which creation groups one contribution carries. A join table — a contribution may have several.

indexes.name: contribution_creation_groups_contribution_id_idx
indexes.note: Redundant with the leading column of uniq_contribution_creation_group. Do not recreate it in gradido2.

notes: Legacy declares no foreign key constraints on this table, only indexes — the convention it inherited from crea_records. Referential integrity is the application's job in legacy; whether gradido2 keeps that is an open decision, see below.
The surrogate id is not used by anything: every access is by (contribution_id, creation_group_id) or by one of them. gradido2 could make the pair the primary key and drop the column.
contributions.creation_groups_set_at is the companion column: while it is NULL an inline '#tag' in the memo still counts, and once it carries a timestamp this table is the only truth.

open.question: Do the join tables get real foreign keys in gradido2?
open.detail: Legacy has none here or in crea_records. A deleted creation group therefore leaves rows pointing at nothing, and both implementations then have to agree on what a dangling row means. A foreign key with ON DELETE CASCADE answers it once in the schema.
open.why_it_matters: Two implementations tidying up dangling rows differently is exactly the class of bug contracts/ exists to prevent.
open.status: unanswered — applies to contribution_creation_groups and crea_records together
